availability: No reviewed availability-rate measurement was retrieved for any London area; only vacancy rates are available, and availability is a distinct definition.
midtown_fringe: Only City Fringe vacancy history is retained (Q3-Q4 2025); Midtown itself remains unmeasured and no current-period Fringe evidence was found.
wider_london: Only selected districts (Hammersmith, VNEB, Stratford) are covered; these samples do not represent all wider London.

claims.text: Semafor (published 9 Oct 2026) reports Canary Wharf Group's office occupancy now exceeds 92%, with local retailer sales 40% above 2019 and visitor numbers on track to beat last year's 76 million record.
claims.headline: Canary Wharf occupancy reported above 92%

claims.text: Semafor reports Visa recently leased 300,000 sq ft, Barclays bought its headquarters for £750m, Citi is investing over $1bn in its European HQ, and JPMorgan proposes a £3bn 265m tower subject to approval.
claims.headline: Canary Wharf tenant commitments reported

claims.text: These Canary Wharf items are attributed secondary reporting of occupier commitments and a proposed scheme; they evidence announced demand and planned status, not completed occupation or consented construction.

Reuters-sourced reporting (5 Oct 2026) says developer LS Estates is sounding out defence and AI companies for a refurbished nine-floor Canary Wharf office formerly used by Credit Suisse support staff.
claims.headline: Canary Wharf refurbishment marketed to defence and AI occupiers

claims.text: The same report states the £100m-plus refit of 17 Columbus Courtyard, backed by GIC and Oaktree, had earmarked up to 60% of space for laboratories but life-sciences interest was lower than expected in the short term.
claims.headline: Life-sciences interest below expectation at 17 Columbus Courtyard

claims.text: Watch whether the 17 Columbus Courtyard refit secures defence, AI or alternative occupiers, and whether the JPMorgan tower proposal advances through planning; both would test Canary Wharf's demand mix.

Knight Frank commentary (published 7 Oct 2026) states London office development activity is not keeping pace with occupier demand for the type of space now required, citing viability pressures and macroeconomic caution.
claims.headline: Knight Frank: development lagging occupier demand

claims.text: Knight Frank's view is attributed commentary without a measurement period; it supports a qualitative supply-constraint narrative rather than a quantified London-office indicator.

London Fire Brigade received Lambeth Council planning permission to refurbish its historic Albert Embankment headquarters to provide a fire station, office space and community spaces (published 6 Oct 2026).
claims.headline: Lambeth permission for Albert Embankment refurbishment

claims.text: The Albert Embankment permission evidences an announced refurbishment plan, not completed works, occupation or a market-wide supply change; the decision date is not established.
Savills reported Central London Q2 2026 take-up of 2.4 million sq ft across 192 transactions, up 0.2 million sq ft (9.1%) on Q1 2026's 2.2 million sq ft.
claims.headline: Central London Q2 take-up 2.4m sq ft

claims.text: Savills reported Central London vacancy fell 0.2 percentage points to 7.2% at end-Q2 2026 from 7.4% at end-Q1 2026; the City rate was unchanged at 7.0%.
claims.headline: Central London vacancy 7.2% at end-Q2 2026

claims.text: Savills reported Central London office supply of 18.7 million sq ft at end-Q2 2026, down 0.4 million sq ft (2.1%) from 19.1 million sq ft at end-Q1 2026.
claims.headline: Reported Central London supply 18.7m sq ft

claims.text: Savills reported H1 2026 Central London Grade A rents of £76.21 per sq ft in the City (up 7% on H1 2025) and £106.17 per sq ft in the West End, from leasing transactions rather than asking rents.
claims.headline: H1 2026 Grade A rents: City £76.21, West End £106.17

claims.text: Savills reported H1 2026 West End average prime rent of £175.10 per sq ft, up 2.3% on H1 2025, and a City prime rent of £116.73 per sq ft, up 19% year-on-year.
claims.headline: H1 2026 prime rents: West End £175.10, City £116.73

claims.text: Savills reported a January-May 2026 average achieved City prime rent of £135 per sq ft and a January-May City Grade A rent of £79.65 per sq ft, up 13% on the same period in 2025.
claims.headline: City January-May prime £135, Grade A £79.65

claims.text: City and West End rent figures use different averaging windows (H1, January-May, quarterly) and transaction averages; they cannot be combined into a single rent trend or read as asking-rent movement.
Savills reported H1 2026 development starts of just 1.5 million sq ft, with only one new-build scheme (Delta at Paddington, 234,000 sq ft) and 14 refurbishment starts.
claims.headline: H1 2026 starts 1.5m sq ft, one new-build

claims.text: Savills reported Q2 2026 Central London development completions of 1.4 million sq ft across 11 new developments and major refurbishments, matching Q1 2026's 1.4 million sq ft.
claims.headline: Q2 2026 completions 1.4m sq ft

claims.text: Savills forecasts Central London development completions reaching 22 million sq ft by end-2029 across 148 schemes, with 28% of that future supply not yet started and vulnerable to delay or withdrawal.
claims.headline: Savills forecasts 22m sq ft completions by 2029

claims.text: Unlet future construction can compete for occupiers even though it is not currently available space; the 28% unstarted share is a delivery-risk qualification, not present supply.
Watch whether H2 2026 development starts recover from the H1 1.5 million sq ft level and whether unstarted pipeline schemes secure funding; both would change the timing of competing supply.
Savills reported the largest Q1 2026 pre-let: Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer's acquisition of British Land and GIC's 1 Appold Street, EC2 (268,000 sq ft) at £104 per sq ft for 21 years.
claims.headline: 1 Appold Street pre-let 268,000 sq ft at £104

claims.text: Savills reported Central London take-up of 600,830 sq ft in May 2026 across 56 transactions, published 30 June 2026 and covering May activity only.
claims.headline: May 2026 take-up 600,830 sq ft

claims.text: BNP Paribas Real Estate reported Grade A space accounted for 78.0% of Central London take-up in Q1 2026, a share of take-up rather than of stock.
claims.headline: Grade A 78% of Q1 2026 take-up

claims.text: Savills reported H1 2026 average rents in BREEAM 'Excellent' or 'Outstanding' buildings were 49% higher than non-rated buildings in the West End and 39% higher in the City.
claims.headline: BREEAM-rated buildings show rent premium

claims.text: The BREEAM premium is a static H1 2026 comparison of average rents; it does not establish a widening gap, a causal amenity effect or pricing power for landlords.
Deutsche Bank announced it will take space at YY London, Canary Wharf, from early 2028, in a fully electric building targeting net-zero-in-operation with rooftop gardens and commuter facilities.
claims.headline: Deutsche Bank plans YY London occupation from 2028

claims.text: The Deutsche Bank item is an announced future occupation plan with a target sustainability performance, not observed occupation or independently verified net-zero achievement.
ONS reported London residents' employment rate of 73.9%, unemployment rate of 6.8% and inactivity rate of 20.5% for the May-July 2026 three-month period (published 15 September 2026).
claims.headline: London May-July 2026: employment 73.9%, unemployment 6.8%

claims.text: These ONS rates are residence-based Labour Force Survey estimates for London residents, not London workplace jobs, office workers or occupier floor-space demand, and are three-month levels rather than weekly changes.

Morgan McKinley's London Employment Monitor reported professional job vacancies in London fell to 4,368 in Q3 2026, down 6% quarter-on-quarter and 11% year-on-year, with monthly vacancies down 30% across the quarter.
claims.headline: London professional vacancies down 11% year-on-year

claims.text: The Morgan McKinley figures are professional recruitment vacancies, a labour-demand indicator distinct from office vacancy or take-up, and remain candidate evidence pending monitoring review.
The Bank of England MPC voted 6-3 on 16 September 2026 to maintain Bank Rate at 3.75%, with three members preferring a 0.25 percentage point increase to 4%.
claims.headline: Bank Rate held at 3.75% on 16 September 2026

claims.text: The Bank of England reported UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August 2026 and said it is likely to rise further over coming quarters.
claims.headline: UK CPI 3.1% in August 2026

claims.text: The Bank of England's stated outlook is that UK CPI inflation is likely to rise further over coming quarters; this is a source forecast, not observed inflation.
GLA Economics reported London real GVA grew 0.3% in 2023 versus 0.4% for the UK, and estimates real GVA rose 1.1% in 2024 and 1.9% in 2025.
claims.headline: GLA: London GVA 0.3% in 2023, estimates for 2024-25

claims.text: The 2023 figure is an observed ONS release reported by GLA; the 2024 and 2025 figures are GLA estimates, not official outturn, and are London-wide context rather than office-market measurement.
ONS reported 28% of workers in Great Britain were hybrid workers between 8 January and 30 March 2025, a survey of working adults rather than London office attendance.
claims.headline: 28% of GB workers hybrid in early 2025

claims.text: The hybrid-work share is Great Britain-wide and dated to early 2025; it is stale contextual evidence and cannot establish current London office attendance or floor-area requirements.
Savills reported Q4 2025 vacancy rates of 26% in Hammersmith and 18% in VNEB, versus 7.0% in the City, 7.9% in the West End and 8.2% in City Fringe.
claims.headline: Q4 2025 vacancy: Hammersmith 26%, VNEB 18%

claims.text: The Q4 2025 district comparison is historical context from selected districts; Hammersmith and VNEB are samples and do not represent all wider London, and City Fringe is not Midtown.
City AM, citing CoStar, reported Hammersmith, the outer edge of London's East End and Hounslow among the worst-performing areas for office space in the capital (published 9 April 2026).
claims.headline: CoStar-cited report flags weak outer-district office performance

claims.text: Lendlease reported the Turing Building at Stratford Cross provides 350,000 sq ft of Grade A office space, the first building delivered under its joint venture with CPP Investments.
claims.headline: Turing Building Stratford 350,000 sq ft Grade A

claims.text: Lendlease reported plans submitted to Newham for Stratford Cross's final phase, proposing about 2,000 homes, a public park, retail space and improved walking and cycling routes (published 20 August 2026).
claims.headline: Stratford Cross final phase plans submitted

claims.text: The Stratford Cross submission is a residential-led proposal, not consented development or completed office supply, though it signals competing land use around an established commercial district.
Watch whether the Stratford Cross final phase is consented and whether the Turing Building's unlet area is disclosed; both would affect competing wider-London supply.

For landlords, the combination of constrained H1 2026 starts, falling reported supply and a 78% Grade A take-up share suggests quality-space competition may persist, but this is a market-level reading, not asset-specific pricing power.

Watch Q3 2026 Central London take-up, vacancy and supply releases and any new availability-rate series; no weekly London office indicator exists, so week-over-week movement cannot be established from current evidence.

limitations: Weekly comparison is not possible: no reviewed source-defined adjacent seven-day London office totals or stock snapshots seven days apart were retrieved, so no week-over-week movement is claimed.

Several current items (Canary Wharf occupancy and tenant commitments, LS Estates marketing, 17 Columbus Courtyard refit) are candidate secondary reporting pending monitoring validation of definitions and measurements.
Central London aggregates do not establish whole-London coverage; UK and Great Britain macro and hybrid data are contextual, not London office measurements.
Rent figures use differing averaging windows and transaction averages, so cross-area or cross-period rent trends cannot be inferred.
